summary: Install-time persistent daemon exfiltrating filesystem data and injecting code into co-tenant packages
details: package.json declares both preinstall and postinstall hooks that run probe.js, which copies daemon.js to /tmp/.npm-helper.js and spawns it as a detached background Node process (stdio 'ignore', unref) that persists beyond npm install for approximately 6 hours. The daemon enumerates /tmp for directories matching AC<32hex>, walks their subdirectories, and POSTs the observed path identifiers (account/service/package names) every 80ms to a hardcoded webhook.site endpoint (https://webhook.site/cc08d9d9-232a-42a2-8d55-0f75cb5e0e67). daemon.js also writes an 'injected-by-other-tenant' node_modules package into other AC<hex> build directories on the same host and appends a payload to any @twilio/runtime-handler package found on disk that reads process.env.ACCOUNT_SID and the first six characters of process.env.AUTH_TOKEN and writes a proof file to /tmp/xtenant-rce-proof.txt. The package.json description and code comments self-label the package as 'Authorized security research probe (bug bounty)' targeting Twilio HackerOne; the shipped behavior is install-time exfiltration, persistence, and cross-package code injection regardless of that labeling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
